title: Anglo-Indian (1...Nf6)
intro: Against 1...Nf6, develop 2.Nc3. Meet ...g6 with g3 and Bg2, ...d5 with cxd5 and g3, and ...e6 with Nf3.

lessons.title: Meeting 2...g6
lessons.summary: Fianchetto with g3 and Bg2 against the King's Indian set-up.

steps.text: 1...Nf6 is Black's most flexible reply to 1.c4. White develops 2.Nc3 to control d5 and e4.

steps.hint: Push c4, then develop the queen's knight.
steps.ifRight: Now White is ready for g3 or Nf3.

steps.text: Black chooses a King's Indian set-up with 2...g6.

steps.ifRight: The bishop will go to g2.

steps.text: Put your bishop on the long diagonal.
steps.hint: Move the f1 bishop to g2.
steps.ifRight: White controls the light squares across the board.

steps.text: Black castles: 4...O-O. Continue with your calm English development.
steps.hint: Develop the king's knight to f3.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.Nf3 (or 5.e4) to prepare O-O and d3.
steps.ifRight: Next come O-O, d3, Rb1 and b4.

lessons.title: Meeting 2...d5
lessons.summary: Trade on d5, play g3 and recapture bxc3.

steps.text: Black challenges c4 in the centre with 2...d5, heading towards a Grünfeld structure.

steps.hint: Capture on d5 with the c-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3.cxd5 to remove Black's centre pawn.
steps.ifRight: White keeps an extra central pawn.

steps.text: Prepare to challenge the d5 knight with your bishop.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.g3 so Bg2 hits the knight on d5.

steps.text: After 4.g3 g6 5.Bg2, Black often trades knights on c3.

steps.ifWrong: Play 6.bxc3 to strengthen d4 and open the b-file for your rook.
steps.ifRight: White builds a strong centre with d4 or Nf3 and O-O.

feedback.d2c3: 6.dxc3 trades queens after ...Qxd1+ and helps Black equalize. Take with bxc3.

lessons.title: Meeting 2...e6
lessons.summary: Develop Nf3 and meet ...Bb4 with Qc2.

steps.text: Black keeps the centre flexible with 2...e6, ready for ...Bb4 or ...d5.
Develop your king's knight first instead of g3, so ...d5 and ...d4 is never annoying.
steps.ifWrong: Play 3.Nf3 to guard d4 and keep all options open.
steps.ifRight: White can meet ...Bb4 cleanly or answer ...d5 with d4.

steps.text: Black pins the c3 knight with 3...Bb4.
Protect c3 with your queen so Black cannot double your pawns.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.Qc2: if Black takes on c3, Qxc3 keeps your pawn structure intact.
steps.ifRight: Next come a3, g3 or e3, keeping the bishop pair.

steps.text: Here Black pushed 3...d5 instead of 3...Bb4. Claim your share of the centre.
steps.ifWrong: Play 4.d4 to transpose into a sound Queen's Gambit.
steps.ifRight: You have a healthy central position with easy development.

steps.text: After 3...Bb4 4.Qc2 O-O, ask the bishop what it wants.
steps.hint: Attack the bishop on b4 with a pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.a3 to win the bishop pair after ...Bxc3 Qxc3.
steps.ifRight: White either gains the bishop pair or wins space with b4.
